newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela labor reform paves way to growth - Petkoff.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela labor reform paves way to growth - Petkoff.

text.p: An agreement to reform Venezuela's severance pay system, hammered out by union, business and government officials this weekend, will pave the way for greater productivity, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said Monday.
"In my opinion, it is one of the changes in the legal tangles of the state which is going to throw open the productive doors of the country," Petkoff said in an interview on Radio Caracas Radio.
The agreement, "means the country can go along a path of growth with fewer obstacles," he said.

The greatest achievement of the agreement, which is to be formally announced at a ceremony by President Rafael Caldera later Monday, was the removal of a retroactivity clause which meant annual severance payments were calculated based on an employee's latest salary.
"Calculating the severance payments annually is going to relieve companies of the tremendous burden of the retroactivity," Petkoff said.
Under the new system, workers will receive 45 days of severance pay after a first year, 60 days after two and two additional days for each year worked up to a maximum of 90 days.
Unlike the previous system, the payments will be made annually in a form chosen by the employee, Petkoff said.
Government, business and union leaders have spent years trying to reform the current system without success.

The new system will be accompanied by an increase in the minimum salary. Petkoff said Caldera would decide on the salary level, which would be not less than 53,000 ($111) per month or more than 90,000 ($188) per month.
The new severance pay system still requires approval by Congress, but Petkoff said all sides involved felt there was enough consensus for it to be approved swiftly.
"Nobody believed this was going to happen...It shows a lot of maturity in the business and labor sectors," he said.
